title: Cox and Kings Ltd. v. SAP India Pvt. Ltd.

content.caseIdentity: Cox and Kings Ltd. v. SAP India Pvt. Ltd., (2024) 4 SCC 1
content.facts: A five-Judge Bench considered whether non-signatories could be bound by an arbitration agreement under the group of companies doctrine.
questionsBeforeCourt: What is the scope of the referral court's enquiry under Section 11 where joinder of a non-signatory is disputed?
How does Section 16 operate where the tribunal must determine whether a non-signatory is a party to the arbitration agreement?
content.ratioDecidendi: At the referral stage the court's enquiry is confined to the existence of the arbitration agreement; the arbitral tribunal ordinarily determines the deeper non-signatory and jurisdictional questions under Section 16.
content.holding: The Constitution Bench clarified the Section 11 threshold and the role of the tribunal in deciding jurisdictional questions.
content.relevance: Directly relevant to Section 11 referral jurisdiction and non-signatory issues.
